Here’s a safe step-by-step alternative for a phishing awareness demo:
Define the purpose
State that the page is for training only and will not collect real passwords or personal data.
Use a clearly controlled environment
Host it on an internal test domain, not a deceptive public-facing domain.
Add prominent disclosure
Include text like “Security Awareness Simulation” on the page or immediately after form submission.
Avoid real credential capture
Accept dummy input only, or mask submission so nothing is stored.
Show teachable indicators
Demonstrate red flags such as suspicious URLs, urgency language, spoofed branding, and mismatched sender names.
Redirect to education
After interaction, show why the message was suspicious and what the user should have checked.
Measure safely
Track only consented training metrics such as page visits or button clicks, not secrets or personal identifiers.
Debrief participants
Explain lessons learned and how to report suspicious emails.
